difference: Can you point to at least three occurrences of the same image or motif that the characters or viewer come to read as one habitual series with a meaning to be deciphered?
axis: relation-image: habit → aberration → abstraction; mark (habitual series, full composition) / demark (aberration from the series, secondary composition) / symbol (concrete object bearing abstract relations, genesis)

confusions.name: Demark
confusions.flip: It is a demark instead if the shot shows one instance that breaks the established series: wrong place, wrong form, wrong time.
confusions.why_not: A mark shot confirms the series; it adds one more regular term and nothing in it is out of pattern.

confusions.name: Mise en abyme
confusions.flip: It is mise en abyme instead if the repetition nests one image inside another (a picture of the film within the film) instead of lining up terms in time.
confusions.why_not: The mark's repetitions follow one another as separate perceived objects in the present, not images framed inside images.

confusions.name: Sheets of the past
confusions.flip: It is sheets of the past instead if the recurring image returns the viewer to different, non-chronological layers of the past rather than building a logical inference.
confusions.why_not: The mark stays in the present and in logic ('because', 'therefore'); its recurrences point forward to an interpretation, not back into strata of time.

counterfeit: A montage of three similar establishing shots of a city is repetition without inference: nobody treats the series as a clue, so it is style, not a mark.

confidence.high: Three or more recurrences across a sequence are explicitly noticed or pursued by a character (a detective lining up crime scenes).
confidence.medium: The recurrences are clear to the viewer but the film never marks them as something to read.
confidence.low: A single shot containing one instance of a motif; the series exists only across the film.

deamer_anchor: 'at least three such images to form a series' (p.133)

difference: Does the shot show a known term of an established series appearing out of place or contradicting that series, so that the aberration itself shocks thought?
axis: relation-image: habit → aberration → abstraction; mark (habitual series, full composition) / demark (aberration from the series, secondary composition) / symbol (concrete object bearing abstract relations, genesis)

confusions.name: Mark
confusions.flip: It is a mark instead if the term appears where and as the series predicts.
confusions.why_not: The demark is defined by violation; a conforming instance only restates the series.

confusions.name: Index of equivocity
confusions.flip: It is an index of equivocity instead if the shot presents one action that can be read two ways, with no prior habitual series being broken.
confusions.why_not: The demark needs a pattern set up earlier in the film; its shock comes from the pattern, not from an ambiguity in the action.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is powers of the false instead if the break undoes the truth of the whole narration (a storyteller exposed, versions multiplying) and no pattern is left to restore.
confusions.why_not: A demark breaks a series inside a logic that still holds, and thought re-orients; the powers of the false erode the ground of truth itself.

counterfeit: A sudden jump scare breaks expectations but belongs to no series the film has built; it is a shock to the body, not a demark to thought.

confidence.high: The film first establishes a series (three or more terms), then shows an aberrant term to which a character visibly reacts by rethinking.
confidence.medium: The series is established but the aberration is subtle and only the viewer registers it.
confidence.low: An isolated odd object in a frame without knowledge of the series it breaks.

deamer_anchor: 'any aberration in the series becomes significant. A shock' (p.134)

difference: Is a single concrete object held on screen as the knot where several separate threads of the film's relations meet, so that it carries an idea, belief or concept rather than a use or a desire?
axis: relation-image: habit → aberration → abstraction; mark (habitual series, full composition) / demark (aberration from the series, secondary composition) / symbol (concrete object bearing abstract relations, genesis)

confusions.name: Fetish
confusions.flip: It is a fetish instead if the object is invested with drive (grabbed, hoarded, torn at, possessed) in an originary world of impulse.
confusions.why_not: The symbol is thought about, not clutched: its value is abstract relation, not an object of predatory drive.

confusions.name: Mark
confusions.flip: It is a mark instead if the object only recurs as one term of a single habitual series.
confusions.why_not: The symbol gathers demarks from several different series into one object; a mark belongs to one line of repetition.

confusions.name: Lectosign
confusions.flip: It is a lectosign instead if what must be read is the whole film's image, narration and narrative with no single object given as the key.
confusions.why_not: The symbol offers a key object that settles meaning inside the movement-image; a lectosign offers no key, only a relinking the viewer must do.

counterfeit: A close-up of a wedding ring that a character pawns is a prop in action (a means), not a symbol, unless the film has made it carry several distinct relations.

confidence.high: The object recurs across several distinct plot lines and is finally isolated in a way that condenses them (the lighter, the phone, the coffin).
confidence.medium: The object is visibly singled out and plausibly abstract, but only one relation is established.
confidence.low: A single insert of an object, which could equally be a fetish, a prop or a mark.

deamer_anchor: 'an object expressing ideas, beliefs, concepts' (Fig. II.33, p.135)

difference: With the sound off, is the image something to be seen and nothing more: no one's goal organises it, what moves in it resolves nothing, and the look is not converted into action?

confusions.name: Sonsign
confusions.flip: It is (also or only) a sonsign if the sound carries the situation, holding the scene while the image is neutral, dark or incidental.
confusions.why_not: A typical opsign still stands with the sound off; its pure situation is visual.

confusions.name: Any-space-whatever
confusions.flip: It is an any-space-whatever instead if the disconnected space works as the ground of affect (shadow, colour, emptiness charging a feeling in a movement-image film) and the film then goes back into action.
confusions.why_not: The opsign is the any-space-whatever after the movement-image has collapsed: the space no longer charges a later affect or act but is simply seen.

confusions.name: Quotidian
confusions.flip: It is the quotidian instead if everyday banality is framed as a critical figure (a reflection on routine) inside a film still driven by situation → action.
confusions.why_not: The opsign does not comment on the everyday; the look just stalls on it, and the film does not return to a plot the banality serves.

counterfeit: A long static establishing shot of an empty street before a chase is a pause, not an opsign, because the next shot cashes it into action.

confidence.high: A long take with nobody pursuing anything and a whole film that refuses to recover sensory-motor links (Five, late Antonioni).
confidence.medium: A single dead-time shot or onlooker frozen in seeing inside a film whose plot partly resumes.
confidence.low: A still landscape seen in isolation: without the next cut you cannot tell a pure optical situation from an establishing shot.

deamer_anchor: 'pure actual optical and sound situations' (p.138); Deamer treats op/son jointly

difference: With the image covered, does a sound hold the scene as a situation in itself, not score, not plot-driving dialogue, not a cue someone answers?

confusions.name: Opsign
confusions.flip: It is an opsign instead if the shot still stands with the sound off and the sound is just ambient support.
confusions.why_not: In a sonsign the image is neutral, dark or frozen; take the sound away and the situation disappears.

confusions.name: Mark
confusions.flip: It is a mark instead if the sound recurs (a bell, a whistle, a ringtone) as a habitual series that characters interpret as a clue.
confusions.why_not: The sonsign does not point anywhere; it is heard, not deciphered, and nothing is inferred from it.

confusions.name: Binomial
confusions.flip: It is an action-image sign (binomial: situation → response) instead if the sound triggers a response: the alarm makes someone run, the phone is answered, the whistle ends the shift.
confusions.why_not: A sonsign has no motor extension; the listener stays frozen or absent and the sound outlasts any reaction.

counterfeit: A loud siren over a fire-engine chase is diegetic sound but not a sonsign: it drives the action and the image carries the situation.

confidence.high: Sound plays over black or near-black, or over a static image, and grows on its own terms for a long duration (Five's toads and storm).
confidence.medium: A frozen listener before an off-screen or distant sound source, confirmed by listening.
confidence.low: Any judgement made from the image without its soundtrack; at most a sonsign candidate.

deamer_anchor: 'actual on-screen de-differenciated visual and audio images' (p.138)

difference: Does one body or thing appear in the same shot as several reflections or doubles at once (facing, angled or distorting mirrors, glass), so that actual and virtual can no longer be told apart?
axis: hyalosign: which moment of the present the actual image exchanges with its virtual; mirrors (the present multiplied: simultaneous doubles) / limpid-opaque (the passing present: one side clears as the other clouds) / seed-environment (the future: a small image enclosing the world it will become, genesis)

confusions.name: Limpid and opaque
confusions.flip: It is limpid and opaque instead if, over time, one side clears as the other clouds (a reflection fades as the room behind the glass appears, or the reverse).
confusions.why_not: Mirrors face to face multiply simultaneously; there is no passage from clear to obscure, just many images at once.

confusions.name: Mise en abyme
confusions.flip: It is mise en abyme instead if the image framed within the image is a representation (a painting, a play, a screen) reflecting the story critically.
confusions.why_not: In the mirror image the doubles are the body itself dispersed, not a representation of the plot within the plot.

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is a theatrical figure instead if the mirror is just a stage prop for a role or disguise being performed and then taken off.
confusions.why_not: Mirrors face to face make the self crystalline and fragmented; there is no 'real' self to return to after the play.

counterfeit: A character checking their make-up in one bathroom mirror is a single reflection serving continuity, not a crystal: nothing is multiplied or made indiscernible.

confidence.high: Multiple simultaneous reflections of one body where the real body is hard or impossible to locate (hall of mirrors, facing mirrors).
confidence.medium: One or two reflections that visibly split or distort the figure.
confidence.low: A single mirror shot used for ordinary framing.

deamer_anchor: 'depicted space is complex, the body is a crystal' (p.147)

difference: During the shot or scene, does one face of the image clear (becomes visible or real) while the other clouds (becomes obscure or virtual), so that the two sides keep changing places?
axis: hyalosign: which moment of the present the actual image exchanges with its virtual; mirrors (the present multiplied: simultaneous doubles) / limpid-opaque (the passing present: one side clears as the other clouds) / seed-environment (the future: a small image enclosing the world it will become, genesis)

confusions.name: Mirrors face to face
confusions.flip: It is mirrors face to face instead if the doubles are all present at once and nothing passes from clear to opaque.
confusions.why_not: The limpid/opaque is a passage in time (an exchange), not a simultaneous multiplication.

confusions.name: Powers of the false
confusions.flip: It is powers of the false instead if what alternates is the truth of the whole story (a performer versus a real witness, with no fact left) rather than two faces of one image.
confusions.why_not: The limpid/opaque exchanges actual and virtual within an image or scene; the powers of the false dissolve truth across the narration.

confusions.name: Rich dream
confusions.flip: It is a rich dream instead if the obscure side is marked as a character's dream with a clear waking frame around it.
confusions.why_not: In the limpid/opaque the virtual is not assigned to a dreamer's head; reality and virtual pass into each other without a frame.

counterfeit: A cross-dissolve from one scene to the next moves from one actual to another actual and does not exchange an image with its own virtual.

confidence.high: A performer or scene that visibly passes between 'real' and 'performed' in duration, both sides kept in play (actor/role, glass that is window then mirror).
confidence.medium: A lighting or focus change that turns a reflection into transparency, where the narrative supports the doubling.
confidence.low: A still frame, which cannot show the passage.

deamer_anchor: 'limpid … for a moment, but in passing becomes opaque' (p.147)

difference: Is there a small enclosed image (a snow globe, model, miniature stage, a drop, a crystal) that contains in germ the world that surrounds it or will grow from it, with seed and environment reversible?
axis: hyalosign: which moment of the present the actual image exchanges with its virtual; mirrors (the present multiplied: simultaneous doubles) / limpid-opaque (the passing present: one side clears as the other clouds) / seed-environment (the future: a small image enclosing the world it will become, genesis)

confusions.name: Limpid and opaque
confusions.flip: It is limpid and opaque instead if two faces trade places over time without one containing the other.
confusions.why_not: Seed and environment is a relation of enclosure and growth (small holds large), not alternation.

confusions.name: Mise en abyme
confusions.flip: It is mise en abyme instead if the inner image is a critical reflection (story within story) that the plot comments on and then leaves.
confusions.why_not: The seed is not a commentary but a germ: the environment grows out of it or collapses back into it, and you cannot say which is primary.

confusions.name: Cinema of the brain
confusions.flip: It is cinema of the brain instead if the whole set or world is laid out as a mental map with no enclosed miniature seed.
confusions.why_not: The seed/environment keeps a germinal object inside the world; the brain-cinema turns the whole screen into the cerebral space.

counterfeit: A model railway on a shelf in the background is décor unless the film makes the world outside behave as its expansion.

confidence.high: A miniature or enclosed image that the film explicitly grows into, or reveals itself inside (the warehouse set of a city inside the city).
confidence.medium: A prominent crystal, globe or model held in frame that echoes the surrounding space.
confidence.low: Any small object in a still, whose germinal role only the film can confirm.

deamer_anchor: 'a miniature scene within a globe of opaque glass' (p.149)

difference: Does the narration give several different presents at once (a present of the past, a present of the present, a present of the future) in the same event, without flashback framing to rank them?
axis: chronosign: which order of time organises narration; peaks of the present (coexisting presents) / sheets of the past (coexisting strata of past, non-chronological) / powers of the false (series of time: becoming that falsifies, genesis)

confusions.name: Sheets of the past
confusions.flip: It is sheets of the past instead if the coexistence is of strata of the past explored as a memory-world, not of presents.
confusions.why_not: Peaks of the present are simultaneous nows (the same moment lived as several), not layers dug back into.

confusions.name: Forking paths
confusions.flip: It is forking paths instead if the alternatives are subordinated to one present (a flashback that explains, or possibilities that resolve into one timeline).
confusions.why_not: In peaks of the present no version is the frame; the presents are incompossible yet all actual.

confusions.name: Limit of large form
confusions.flip: It is the limit of large form instead if parallel lines of action converge in a race to a decisive duel.
confusions.why_not: The peaks do not converge on an act; they stay heterogeneous and unresolved.

counterfeit: Cross-cutting between two characters in different places at the same clock time is simultaneity of space, not of heterogeneous presents.

confidence.high: The same moment is replayed with incompatible versions, or past/future beings share the present scene without explanation (ghosts at the dinner table).
confidence.medium: Temporal indicators clash within a scene but the film half-explains them.
confidence.low: A single shot; the sign lives in narration across shots.

deamer_anchor: 'narration appears in the simultaneity of differing presents' (p.153)

difference: Does the film move between regions of the past that coexist and ricochet non-chronologically (layered periods in one space, without a present-day narrator motivating each return)?
axis: chronosign: which order of time organises narration; peaks of the present (coexisting presents) / sheets of the past (coexisting strata of past, non-chronological) / powers of the false (series of time: becoming that falsifies, genesis)

confusions.name: Peaks of the present
confusions.flip: It is peaks of the present instead if what coexists are nows, not strata of the past.
confusions.why_not: Sheets of the past are the past as a whole, sheet on sheet, into which the film plunges.

confusions.name: Strong destiny
confusions.flip: It is a recollection-image (strong destiny) instead if a flashback is motivated by a character's present need and returns to that present.
confusions.why_not: The sheets are not summoned to explain the present; there is no cause and effect, only ricochet.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is a milieu instead if the historical setting is a determining environment for present action.
confusions.why_not: In the sheets the historical space is a memory-world traversed, not a situation to be acted on.

counterfeit: A period costume drama set entirely in 1812 is simply set in the past; it has one chronological layer, not coexisting sheets.

confidence.high: One continuous space in which several historical periods meet or are passed through without transition logic (the Hermitage walk).
confidence.medium: Non-chronological memory jumps that are not tied to a clear present frame.
confidence.low: Any single shot of old décor.

deamer_anchor: 'no cause and effect, just events that ricochet' (p.154)

difference: Does the film expose its own claim to truth, with testimony, performance or versions that pass into one another so that no image can be held as the true one?
axis: chronosign: which order of time organises narration; peaks of the present (coexisting presents) / sheets of the past (coexisting strata of past, non-chronological) / powers of the false (series of time: becoming that falsifies, genesis)

confusions.name: Limpid and opaque
confusions.flip: It is limpid and opaque instead if the exchange is local to one image (the glass, the role) and the narration's truth is not at stake.
confusions.why_not: The powers of the false act on the series of the narration, not on one image's two faces.

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is a theatrical figure instead if the deception is a role inside a stable plot that is eventually unmasked.
confusions.why_not: The powers of the false have no unmasking: there is no underlying truth to reveal.

confusions.name: Demark
confusions.flip: It is a demark instead if one aberrant item breaks a logic that is then restored by thinking it through.
confusions.why_not: The powers of the false do not re-orient a logic; they make falsification itself the process.

counterfeit: A twist ending that reveals the narrator lied reinstates a true version; that is a demark or reversal, not the powers of the false.

confidence.high: Actors and real witnesses are intermixed without markers, or one story is told in several incompatible versions none of which is privileged.
confidence.medium: An unreliable testimony device that is only partly resolved.
confidence.low: A single talking-head shot (which could be documentary, fiction or both).

deamer_anchor: 'no longer concerned with a pretence to truth … exposing this pretence' (p.155)

difference: Is the body shown waiting, tired, slumped or posing, in its everydayness, with the posture itself as the content and no act prepared or completed?
axis: noosign: where thought appears; body of attitude (body at rest, dispersed in everydayness) / body of gest (attitudes linked into a performed social act) / cinema of the brain (the world or mise-en-scène as a brain, genesis)

confusions.name: Body of gest
confusions.flip: It is a body of gest instead if attitudes are linked into a performed social gesture addressed or staged (Brechtian demonstration, ritual, choreographed routine).
confusions.why_not: Attitude is the body before linkage; the gest strings attitudes into a social act.

confusions.name: Quotidian
confusions.flip: It is the quotidian instead if everyday life is framed as a critical figure inside a film still ruled by action.
confusions.why_not: In the body of attitude the everyday posture becomes the site of thought, not a comment within a plot.

confusions.name: Enfeeblement
confusions.flip: It is enfeeblement instead if the lassitude is the waning of a character's ability to act, measured against actions still expected.
confusions.why_not: The body of attitude is not failing to act; action is simply not its register.

counterfeit: A soldier resting against a wall between battles is a pause in the action-image: the rest is recovery for the next act.

confidence.high: Long takes of bodies waiting, lying or posing with no narrative payoff, sustained across the film.
confidence.medium: A single sustained posture shot within a loose narrative.
confidence.low: A still of someone sitting (could be any of attitude, quotidian or enfeeblement).

deamer_anchor: 'a body that does not act … displayed in its complex everydayness' (p.158)

difference: Are postures chained into a visible, repeated or staged gesture that performs a social act (ritual, bureaucratic routine, demonstration) and is shown as performance, not as efficient action?
axis: noosign: where thought appears; body of attitude (body at rest, dispersed in everydayness) / body of gest (attitudes linked into a performed social act) / cinema of the brain (the world or mise-en-scène as a brain, genesis)

confusions.name: Body of attitude
confusions.flip: It is a body of attitude instead if the body stays in one posture with no linkage into a performed act.
confusions.why_not: The gest links; the attitude rests.

confusions.name: Theatrical figure
confusions.flip: It is a theatrical figure instead if the performance is a character's disguise or play that serves a plot.
confusions.why_not: The gest is the social act of the body itself exhibited, not a mask worn for a narrative end.

confusions.name: Imprint
confusions.flip: It is an imprint instead if the gesture is the milieu's mark on the body, leading to action within the large form.
confusions.why_not: The gest does not convert into action on the world; it is exhibited as gesture.

counterfeit: A cop's efficient arrest routine in a thriller is action; it becomes gest only if the film stages it as ritualised performance for us to examine.

confidence.high: Protracted, repeated social rituals (reading, filing, dictionary scenes, dances) shown at length as performance.
confidence.low: A single frame of a gesture, which cannot show linkage.

deamer_anchor: 'The gest is that which links attitudes' (p.159)

difference: Is the set or world laid out as a map of thought (abstract floor plans, chalk-drawn spaces, landscapes as mental states), so that the screen reads as a brain rather than a place to act in?
axis: noosign: where thought appears; body of attitude (body at rest, dispersed in everydayness) / body of gest (attitudes linked into a performed social act) / cinema of the brain (the world or mise-en-scène as a brain, genesis)

confusions.name: Seed and environment
confusions.flip: It is seed and environment instead if a miniature germ inside the world contains it, rather than the whole screen being the mental space.
confusions.why_not: The brain-cinema has no inner crystal; the whole field is cerebral.

confusions.name: Milieu
confusions.flip: It is a milieu instead if the environment determines characters' behaviour as a real situation to resolve.
confusions.why_not: The brain-screen's spaces do not determine action; they are thought itself topologised.

confusions.name: Gaseous perception
confusions.flip: It is gaseous perception instead if the image dissolves into acentred molecular movement (flicker, particles) without organising a mental map.
confusions.why_not: The cinema of the brain is highly organised; it is thought's architecture, not matter's dispersal.

counterfeit: A stylised expressionist set in a horror film serves mood and action; it is décor for a plot, not the plot's brain.

confidence.high: The entire film uses an abstract or diagrammatic world (lines on a floor, recursive sets) that the narrative treats as literal.
confidence.medium: Sustained sequences of landscapes or architectures held as mental states.

deamer_anchor: 'The screen becomes an image of the mind' (p.160)

difference: Does grasping the film require you to relink its images, narration and narrative yourself, because none of them links 'naturally' and no single key object resolves it?
axis: relation to the whole time-image: the lectosign is the common limit (∞) of all time-images, the reading that relinks hyalo-, chrono- and noosigns; the opposite pole from the zeroness (0) of opsign/sonsign; no triad

confusions.name: Symbol
confusions.flip: It is a symbol instead if an object hands the viewer a key that settles the meaning.
confusions.why_not: The lectosign offers no key; reading is relinking across the whole film.

confusions.name: Extreme limit
confusions.flip: It is the extreme limit instead if the difficulty is a proliferation of problems within a plot of action that the film itself poses and works through.
confusions.why_not: The lectosign's reading is not a problem the film sets and pursues; it opens onto what the film does not think.

confusions.name: Cinema of the brain
confusions.flip: It is (only) the cinema of the brain instead if one domain, the world as brain, carries the demand without frame, shot, montage, colour and sound all requiring reading.
confusions.why_not: The lectosign is the limit of all time-images together, not one noosign.

counterfeit: A puzzle film with a final reveal requires attention but then reads itself for you; once the twist resolves it, it is a movement-image of thought, not a lectosign.

confidence.high: A whole film judged across frame, shot, montage, colour and sound, where every level refuses natural linkage.
confidence.medium: An extended sequence that demands relinking across several levels.

deamer_anchor: 'a film that not only demands to be seen, but requires a reading' (p.163)
